citations.assessment: Yoma explains the contextual tractate correction and has two forms of the name. At the question it gives the title with ben; at the resolution it gives optional ben in brackets. Preserve the differences from Heilprin’s wording.
The Nedarim teaching has the distinctive place-name construction ish Uza. Listing parallel names here does not itself establish identity.

holds.reason: The checked Bavli gives Yehoshua with patronymic variation. The Hoshia reading and siglum remain open. A superficially similar form in the Sefaria Variants on Yoma record belongs to the Tosefta apparatus for a different passage and gives no evidence here.

notes.text: Yoma distinctly gives titled Yehoshua ben Uzaa in the question and Yehoshua with optional ben in the resolution. Nedarim has ish Uza. The Hoshia reading and formula remain qualified in this entry.
